commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified or negative, out_string() already knows
the exact string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of
scanning again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

Treat a negative precision in the format string as an omitted
precision, like a negative precision argument already is.

Closes #23019

mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time
of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also
makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the
output failed because out of disk space or similar.

Drop the redundant negative-precision clamp in formatf(). A negative
precision argument reaches out_string(), which treats a negative
precision as an omitted one, as POSIX requires.

Verified by test 2380
Closes #23112

coupling: The defect is split across two mprintf maintenance commits and is reachable only from their composition. Commit c1011df (edit A) widens the out_string() fast-path gate from 'prec == -1' to 'prec < 0' so that any negative precision takes the trusting stream_run() emitter, which emits len bytes; for prec < -1, len was computed as (size_t)prec, i.e. a near-SIZE_MAX length. At the time of edit A this is provably unreachable: formatf() still clamps every negative precision *argument* to -1, and the same commit also normalizes a negative *literal* precision to -1 in parse_flags(), so 'prec < 0' is exactly 'prec == -1' and the diff is behavior-preserving (and it closes the only alternate source of negative literal precisions, so no later format string can smuggle one in either). Commit aaed343 (edit B), a later POSIX-cleanup commit, removes the now-'redundant' negative-precision clamp in formatf(); on its own this is also safe and POSIX-correct, because with the original 'prec == -1' gate a negative precision (e.g. -2 from %.*s) falls into the NUL-aware stream_zrun() scan, which stops at the string terminator and emits strlen() bytes -- exactly the documented 'a negative precision is taken as if the precision were omitted' behavior. Only with BOTH edits does a negative precision argument reach stream_run() with len = (size_t)-2: the asprintf sink's first-chunk memcpy of 512 bytes then reads past a short heap string (ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ in alloc_addrun via curl_maprintf("%.*s", -2, str)). A correct fix is non-local: reverting only edit A's gate leaves the clamp removal in place (safe), and reverting only edit B's clamp removal leaves the widened gate unreachable (safe); fixing either single diff alone suffices, but no single edited diff is 'the bug' -- each is individually correct maintenance, and the vulnerability exists solely in their combination.
